messages.subject: 3D transformations in Cytoscape
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paul and everyone else,

I'm looking at data structures in three dimensions.  Cytoscape is great for graphing node attributes but doesn't do 3D at present.  But one can set position from a three dimensional matrix using RCytoscape as follows:

setPosition (nb.window, as.character(cf$Gene.Name), 3dcoords[,1], 3dcoords[,2])
   fitContent (nb.window)
   showGraphicsDetails (nb.window, TRUE)
setPosition (nb.window, as.character(cf$Gene.Name), 3dcoords[,1], 3dcoords[,3])
setPosition (nb.window, as.character(cf$Gene.Name), 3dcoords[,2], 3dcoords[,3])
   fitContent (nb.window)

This looks at the data from different angles.

Package (rgl) has a rotate3d function:

#  rotate3d(obj, angle, x, y, z, matrix, ...)
#   rotate by 45 degrees about the y axis
setPosition (nb.window, as.character(cf$Gene.Name), 3dcoords[,1], 3dcoords[,2])
nb45 <- rotate3d(3dcoords, pi/4, 0, 1, 0)
setPosition (nb.window, as.character(cf$Gene.Name), nb45[,1], nb45[,2])

This looks at the data from intermediate angles.

For a 3D perspective, it would be good to set both node opacity and node size according to the z dimension.  Node opacity can be done like this:

# setNodeOpacityDirect(obj, node.names, new.value)
scaleop = scale(nb45[,3], scale=T, center=T)
nodeop = 255*scale((scaleop + abs(min(scaleop))), scale=(max(scaleop) + abs(min(scaleop))), center=FALSE)
setNodeOpacityDirect(nb.window, as.character(cf$Gene.Name), nodeop)
# WORKS!  But have to have a colored background to visualize, if nodes are white

Since I set node size and color according to an attribute from the data set (which has biological meaning), it would be good to be able to set node size based on an existing node size, modifying the existing node size.  The function:

# setNodeSizeDirect(obj, node.names, new.size)

appears to require a single integer for new size. I tried to give it (new.size) as a vector and this didn't work.  So, I have two requests to accomplish the goal of setting the node size to render a 3D perspective:

 getNodeSize(); setNodeSizeDirect() with new.sizes as vector

(Both functions would have to handle vectors.) Since I envision making a series of views for a 3D movie, using setNodeSizeRule seems kludgy, since at present it requires uploading an attribute for each case; a smooth movie requires lots of perspectives and the attribute list would rapidly become unwieldy. (Also, as I mentioned, I want a particular attribute to set size and color, which has biological meaning.) If we could set the node size directly by multiplying a vector of the existing node sizes by the z dimension (similar to that done for opacity above), 3D visualization could be simply accomplished and compelling to the eye. Does this make sense and sound reasonable?

Thanks,

Mark Grimes

messages.subject: Re: 3D transformations in Cytoscape
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

Nice use of RCy, rgl and (of course) Cytoscape itself!  Using opacity and size together to indicate depth is very cool.

The current version of RCy 1.5.25 -- which will be released as version 1.6.0 by Bioconductor next Monday, April 2nd, has one of the two methods you want.

Here's how it works for me:

   setNodeSizeDirect (cw, c ('A', 'B', 'C'), c (10, 30, 50))
   redraw (cw)

With a little luck, maybe Jan can create the CytoscapeRPC handler for

   getNodeSize (cw, <list.of.node.ids>)

What version of RCy are you running?  Do you need a pre-release version to solve your immediate needs?

- Paul

messages.subject: Re: 3D transformations in Cytoscape
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

Would you find a setNodeOpacityRule () function useful?  If the z dimension was also a node attribute, then

   setNodeOpacityRule (cw, 'z', c (-100, 0, 100), c (40, 255, 40), mode='interpolate')

might give you some control.

(My example might be lame:  it dims out all nodes which are not at z=0.)

Cytoscape distinguishes three kinds of node opacity:  for the fill color, for the border, and for the font label.  I am considering providing access to this level of control like this:

  setNodeOpacityRule (cw, 'z', c (-100, 0, 100), c (40, 255, 40), mode='interpolate', aspect='all')

where other legal values of aspects includes any combination of  'fill', 'label' and 'border'.

  aspect='all'  would be the same as aspect=c('fill', 'border', 'label')

Your thoughts?

 - Paul

messages.subject: Re: 3D transformations in Cytoscape
messages.body_plain:
Paul

Yes, setNodeOpacityRule() would be an alternative.  But the z
dimension isn't really an attribute, in the same way that node
position is not an attribute.

I envision node position, including the z dimension, as only a
transient thing.  Imagine that you wish to make a movie that rotates a
three dimensional structure in 3D.  This may involve hundreds of
frames.  If you wish to move the data structure in a for: loop, the
technique would have to create an attribute, then delete the attribute
in the next iteration, or else create hundreds of new attributes, and
this would slow down RCy and Cy considerably.  This seems possible,
but not efficient.

A simpler solution might look like this:

	currentsizes <- getNodeSize(cw, node.id.list)
OR (since that is not possible at present):
	currentsizes <- getNodeSizeFromNodeSizeRule(cw, node.id.list,
control.points, node.sizes, mode="interpolate")
	modified.sizes <- currentsizes*3dcorrds[,3] # or some transformation
based on z dimension using scale() as described below
	setNodeSizeDirect (cw, node.id.list, modified.sizes)

In other words,  getNodeSizeFromNodeSizeRule() could substitute for
getNodeSize that must read from Cytoscape.  I have no idea how that
might be implemented but it seems workable.  Does this make sense?

Mark

messages.subject: RCy::getNodeSize (); was Re: 3D transformations in Cytoscape
messages.subject_clean: RCy::getNodeSize (); was Re: 3D transformations in Cytoscape
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

Thanks to Jan, we now have access to node size.  There's a wrinkle:   node width and height may be different.  So I return parallel vectors, as you will see below.
Does this give you what you need?

- Paul

test.getNodeSize = function () {
 title = 'test.getNodeSize'
 window.prep (title)
 cw = new.CytoscapeWindow (title, graph=RCytoscape::makeSimpleGraph ())
 displayGraph (cw)
 layoutNetwork (cw, 'jgraph-spring')

    # establish a good starting point
 lockNodeDimensions (cw, TRUE)
 setNodeSizeDirect (cw, nodes (cw@graph), rep (100, 3))
 redraw (cw)

 sizes =  getNodeSize (cw, nodes (cw@graph))
 checkEquals (sizes$width, c (100, 100, 100))
 checkEquals (sizes$height, c (100, 100, 100))

 setNodeSizeDirect (cw, c ('A', 'B'), 150); redraw (cw)
 sizes =  getNodeSize (cw, nodes (cw@graph))

 checkEquals (sizes$width, c (150, 150, 100))
 checkEquals (sizes$height, c (150, 150, 100))

 setNodeSizeDirect (cw, c ('A', 'B'), c (180, 32));   redraw (cw)

 sizes = getNodeSize (cw, nodes (cw@graph))
 checkEquals (sizes$width, c (180, 32, 100))
 checkEquals (sizes$height, c (180, 32, 100))

    # allow for non-symmetric dimensions: width and height are set separately
 lockNodeDimensions (cw, FALSE)
 setNodeHeightDirect (cw, c ('A', 'B', 'C'), c (12, 22, 32))
 setNodeWidthDirect (cw, c ('A', 'B', 'C'), c (120, 122, 132))
 redraw (cw)

 sizes = getNodeSize (cw, 'B')
